card.name: Verb after a drug's brand name
card.fires_on: The verb 'is' (sometimes 'can') right after a drug or product name used as the sentence subject, in prescribing-information text. It marks the start of a statement about indication, use or approval.

modes.label: Brand name then 'is'
modes.description: 'is' follows an all-caps brand name and begins a statement about what the drug is or is for.
modes.example: Risks Associated with Combination Treatment TAFINLAR<< is>> indicated

modes.label: Product description then 'is'
modes.description: 'is' or 'can' follows a generic name or product description and leads into use or administration.
modes.example: Podofilox Topical Solution 0.5%<< is>> applied to the warts with an applic

card.plain: It marks the little verb that follows a drug's name when a label begins a statement such as 'X is indicated for'.
